subject: principles-of-accounts
title: Absorption and Marginal Costing: Where the Fixed Overhead Goes Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says Absorption and marginal costing always report the same profit, because fixed production overhead is a period cost under both methods. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the method chosen can never change profit

The methods differ on timing: marginal costing expenses the full $12,000 of fixed production overhead in the period, but absorption costing attaches $12 per unit to inventory, so the 200 unsold units carry 200 x $12 = $2,400 of fixed overhead forward in closing inventory - which is why absorption profit of $9,400 exceeds marginal profit of $7,000 by exactly that $2,400 deferral.
Absorption costing reports lower profit whenever inventory rises
The difference comes from the selling price, not the costing method

questions.misconception: Absorption and marginal costing always report the same profit, because fixed production overhead is a period cost under both methods.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Absorption and marginal costing always report the same profit, because fixed production overhead is a period cost under both methods. Reteach point: The methods differ on timing: marginal costing expenses the full $12,000 of fixed production overhead in the period, but absorption costing attaches $12 per unit to inventory, so the 200 unsold units carry 200 x $12 = $2,400 of fixed overhead forward in closing inventory - which is why absorption profit of $9,400 exceeds marginal profit of $7,000 by exactly that $2,400 deferral.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain where fixed production overhead goes under marginal costing.
questions.answer: Under marginal costing the full $12,000 of fixed production overhead is charged as a period cost in the period it is incurred.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the period charge: marginal costing expenses all of the fixed production overhead at once and keeps it out of the unit cost.

questions.prompt: Production is 1,000 units, sales are 800 units and fixed overhead is $12 per unit. How much fixed overhead sits in closing inventory under absorption costing?
questions.feedback: Scene 3 shows the calculation: 200 unsold units x $12 per unit = $2,400 carried forward in closing inventory.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, reconcile marginal profit of $7,000 with absorption profit of $9,400.
questions.answer: Absorption profit is higher by exactly the $2,400 of fixed overhead deferred in closing inventory: $7,000 + $2,400 = $9,400.
questions.feedback: A strong answer gives the full reconciliation in order - $7,000, plus the $2,400 deferral, equals $9,400.
